results.title: U.S. Treasury yields: investors await more economic data
results.content:
U.S. Treasury yields declined on Thursday as investors awaited more economic data, after September's consumer price inflation reading came in stronger than expected in the previous session.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield last fell 9 basis points to 5.099%, while the 30-year Treasury bond yield was down over 8 basis points to 5.439%. The 2-year Treasury note yield was 6 basis points lower to 4.74%.

One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions. [...] Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3% monthly and 2.6% annually, compared with estimates of 0.2% and 2.5%.

The print was already expected to be strong due to soaring energy prices, with gasoline costs up 9.1% and accounting for half of the gain in headline CPI. The energy index also jumped 5.2%.

Investors will now await the producer price index, retail sales data for September and weekly initial jobless claims figures, all due later in the session.

results.title: Treasury yields steady, Trump takes diplomatic tone on Iran
results.content:
Bond yields largely steadied Friday morning as investors digested the latest Treasury auction and President Donald Trump's pledge not to attack Iran until after the midterm elections.

Yields on 10-year U.S. Treasurys — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — were last seen flat at 5.2399%.

The yield on longer-dated 30-year U.S. Treasury notes — which tend to move on geopolitical events — was also unchanged at 5.6150%. [...] The yield on the 2-year Treasury note, which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve rate decisions, was more than 2 basis points higher at 4.7827%.

One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another.

The moves come after Treasury yields fell during the previous session, having hit their highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

results.title: Treasury Yields Slide to Three-Week Lows as Oil Prices Fall - WSJ
results.content:
Ten-year Treasury and German Bund yields slid to multiweek lows in early European trade on Thursday as bond investors absorbed higher-than-expected U.S. inflation data that had prompted a temporary but sharp bond selloff on Wednesday.

Ten- and 30-year U.S. Treasury yields fell to three-week lows of 5.087% and 5.431%, respectively, while the 10-year German Bund yield hit a two-week low of 3.382%, according to Tradeweb data.
